mcq.question: Why does `make_discount` capture `percent` by value (`[percent]`) and not by reference (`[&percent]`)?

options.A: The returned lambda outlives the call; a reference to the parameter would dangle
options.B: Capturing by reference is not allowed in returned lambdas
options.C: Capture by value makes the lambda faster
options.D: Function parameters cannot be captured by reference

mcq.explanation: `percent` is destroyed when `make_discount` returns. A lambda that refers to it would read a dead object. Capturing by value copies it into the lambda.

mcq.question: Which of these can a `std::function<long long(long long)>` NOT hold?

options.A: A function that takes two parameters
options.C: A plain function `long long f(long long)`
options.D: An object with `long long operator()(long long) const`

mcq.explanation: `std::function` stores any callable with a compatible call signature, whether it is a function, a lambda or a function object. A callable needing two arguments does not match.
